item.title: Two Prosecuters | Arthouse Now — Thu Oct 8, 7:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
Adapted from a novel by Soviet writer/political prisoner Georgy Demidov and set in the Soviet Union in 1937, Two Prosecutors follows the attempts of an idealistic government-appointed prosecutor to expose the mistreatment of a dissident Bolshevik writer who has been jailed and tortured without evidence of wrongdoing. He soon realizes the lack of cause for the man's imprisonment isn’t unique under Stalin, and the young lawyer’s moral righteousness may be putting himself in danger. Constructed with a patient yet unmistakable sense of mounting dread, the film exposes how the minutiae of everyday enables fascism’s function. [118 min; drama; Russian and Ukrainian with English subtitles]
Source: Pillar Arts Community Calendar

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Fri Oct 9 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Fri Oct 9 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Fri Oct 9 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: Flights & Flannels — Sat Oct 10, 11:00 AM — Oliver Winery
item.description:
Cozy up, Bloomington — it's time to break out your best flannel and soak in leaf peeping at its finest. Flights & Flannels Weekend trades summer patios for crackling fires, golden hillsides, and the coziest wine weekend of the season. Our Apple Pie Frosé is back - frozen, spiced, and made for sipping on a crisp fall afternoon. S'more season is here too, enjoyed two ways: settle in for our fan-favorite tableside s'mores, or grab a s'more kit to enjoy out on the grounds - fireside or fireside-adjacent, there's no wrong way to get your fix. Cool off with cider buckets, on special and made for sharing. Enjoy live music as Black Orchid sets the mood on the patio from 3-5pm for a perfect fall afternoon. Wear your coziest flannel, bring your people, and settle in for an afternoon built for crisp air, warm fires, and good wine!
Source: Visit Bloomington

item.title: Chinese Tidings: "The Belt and Road Initiative: Domestic Policymaking and Global Impacts" — Tue Oct 13, 6:00 PM
item.description: Pizza is served at 5:30 pm. and the lecture starts at 6:00 pm.About the lecture: Launched in 2013, the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) occupies a central position in China's contemporary foreign policy and domestic development agenda. While often described as an infrastructure investment program, the BRI encompasses multiple dimensions of development policymaking, trade and investment facilitation, financial cooperation, and people-to-people exchange. Understanding how the initiative is organized and implemented is crucial for making sense of China's evolving position in the global economic and political system. This lecture provides a framework for understanding the BRI, with particular attention to its domestic organizing mechanisms, how they shape China's engagement with partner countries, and the broader implications of the initiative for global development.About the presenter: Dr. Hong Zhang is an Assistant Professor in the Department of International Studies at the Hamilton Lugar

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Thu Oct 15 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Thu Oct 15 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Thu Oct 15 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. item.title: Remembering the Climate Crisis — Thu Oct 15, 4:30 PM — INDIANA MEMORIAL UNION (UNION BUILDING)
item.description:
Presentation Abstract: Minority groups are more vulnerable to the impacts of climate change than the rest of the population. Latinx people are the largest growing minority in Indianapolis, yet little is known about how the local effects of climate change in the city impact this population. In this talk, Martell presents the preliminary findings of a study about how Latinx people in Indianapolis think about, feel, and remember climate change as well as their reactions to it. The goal is to develop policy recommendations and provide insights for future educational interventions about climate change education and advocacy.
Source: IU La Casa Latino Cultural Center
